lines.text: Thursday night, crisps in hand, Rosa swears: "I'll start MONDAY."
Nia smirks. You've said it too. And there's DATA on it.
But "I'll start Monday" isn't just an EXCUSE.
In 2014, researchers found Google searches for 'diet' peak every new WEEK, month and year.

post.title: Why "I'll Start Monday" Isn't Just an Excuse #shorts
post.description: Rosa swears she'll start the gym on Monday. Turns out that's a real pattern: Hengchen Dai, Katherine Milkman and Jason Riis (2014, Management Science, "The Fresh Start Effect: Temporal Landmarks Motivate Aspirational Behavior") found Google searches for "diet" peaked at the start of each week, month and year; university gym visits rose at the start of a new week, month and semester and after birthdays; and commitment contracts on stickK rose after the same kinds of landmarks. They call it the fresh start effect. Caveat: the study shows people START more after landmarks, not that those starts last longer. #psychology #shorts #habits #motivation
